//: Vercel reads this from the repository root, which is what makes it useful:
with no config, Vercel sees a pnpm workspace and runs the root build, which
builds every package — including the NestJS API. That is what failed the
first deploy on `nest build`, and it was never going to succeed, because the
API has no business being built to put a static site online.
Naming the build here does the same job as setting Root Directory in the
dashboard, and it lives in git where it can be reviewed instead of in a
//framework: null, not 'nextjs'. next.config.ts sets output: 'export', so the build
leaves a folder of files rather than a server for Vercel to run. Declaring
the framework would have Vercel look for a Next.js server that is not there.
//headers: The same protections as apps/web/public/_headers, which Vercel does not
read — _headers is a Cloudflare convention. Deploying here without this
block would have quietly shipped the site with none of them.
Keep the two in step. They exist twice because the site can be hosted in
either place, not because either is optional.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; media-src 'self' https:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'
